dialect.detail: GnuCOBOL/OpenCOBOL targeting a Linux/Unix environment; uses C$JUSTIFY intrinsic call typical of GnuCOBOL/ACUCOBOL compatibility layer; Italian-language business application with LINE SEQUENTIAL files and .sl/.fd copybook conventions common in Italian ERP/WMS systems

purpose.domain_detail: Warehouse management / logistics: extraction and CSV summary of UTF (Unità di Trasporto Ferroviario or similar) outbound shipping notes (bolle di scarico) with LBX causale and negative stock movement
purpose.summary: This program extracts and summarizes outbound shipping notes (bolle UTF scarico) from a warehouse management system into a CSV file. It reads movement and order files, filters records by causale LBX with negative stock movement, accumulates weights, and sends the result via email. It also updates a counter tracking the last processed shipping note number for three series (S1, S2, S3).

notable_features: Heavy use of COPY statements (27 copybooks) for file definitions
DECLARATIVES section with USE AFTER ERROR for record locking
SET condition-name usage for flags (RecLocked, tutto-ok, trovato, aggiornaContatore)
ACCEPT from ENVIRONMENT for email parameters
INSPECT REPLACING for leading zero suppression
Three series of shipping note ranges (S1/S2/S3) processed sequentially
verdict.notes: No ENVIRONMENT DIVISION header is present (only SPECIAL-NAMES and INPUT-OUTPUT SECTION), which is unusual but valid. The file references many external copybooks (.sl, .fd, .cpy, .def) not shown, limiting full analysis. The C$JUSTIFY call and .sl file conventions suggest an Italian SME ERP/WMS system possibly built on GnuCOBOL or a compatible runtime. Could also be ACUCOBOL given C$JUSTIFY, but GnuCOBOL is more likely given open-source context.
